title: Impact of Grade Retention on Future Academic Performance

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) is the appropriate method here. Students are retained based on a cutoff in their end-of-year test scores (running variable), creating a quasi-random assignment around the threshold. The key assumption is that students just below and just above the cutoff are similar in all characteristics except for the treatment assignment, allowing us to estimate the causal effect of grade retention.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s97_data.csv")

# Examine the data structure
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))

# Determine the cutoff (where treatment probability jumps)
# Check treatment assignment around different potential cutoffs
cutoff_candidates <- seq(-0.5, 0.5, by = 0.01)
treatment_probs <- sapply(cutoff_candidates, function(c) {
  below <- data$running_var < c
  above <- data$running_var >= c
  if(sum(below) > 0 & sum(above) > 0) {
    mean(data$treated[above]) - mean(data$treated[below])
  } else {
    0
  }
})

# Find cutoff with largest treatment probability jump
optimal_cutoff <- cutoff_candidates[which.max(treatment_probs)]
print(paste("Identified cutoff:", optimal_cutoff))

# Center the running variable around the cutoff
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - optimal_cutoff

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                       x = data$running_var_centered, 
                       c = 0)

print("=== MAIN RDD RESULTS ===")
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract and print key coefficient
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
se <- rdd_result$se[1]
pvalue <- rdd_result$pv[1]

print(paste("Treatment Effect (Grade Retention):", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(se, 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(pvalue, 4)))

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Different bandwidth
rdd_half_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                        x = data$running_var_centered, 
                        c = 0, 
                        h = rdd_result$bws[1]/2)
print(paste("Half bandwidth effect:", round(rdd_half_bw$coef[1], 4)))

# 2. Different polynomial order
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                     x = data$running_var_centered, 
                     c = 0, 
                     p = 2)
print(paste("Quadratic specification effect:", round(rdd_quad$coef[1], 4)))

# 3. Check for manipulation (McCrary test)
print("\n=== MANIPULATION TEST ===")
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var_centered, c = 0)
print(paste("Density test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4)))

# 4. Placebo test at false cutoff
false_cutoff_data <- data[data$running_var_centered > 0.1 | data$running_var_centered < -0.1, ]
if(nrow(false_cutoff_data) > 50) {
  placebo_test <- rdrobust(y = false_cutoff_data$y, 
                           x = false_cutoff_data$running_var_centered, 
                           c = 0.05)
  print(paste("Placebo test effect:", round(placebo_test$coef[1], 4)))
  print(paste("Placebo test p-value:", round(placebo_test$pv[1], 4)))
}

# Visualization
pdf("rdd_plot.pdf", width = 10, height = 6)
rdplot(y = data$y, 
       x = data$running_var_centered, 
       c = 0,
       title = "RDD: Effect of Grade Retention on Future Test Scores",
       x.label = "End-of-Year Test Score (Centered)",
       y.label = "Future Test Score")
dev.off()

print("\nRDD plot saved as 'rdd_plot.pdf'")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative treatment effect of approximately -0.15 to -0.25 standard deviations. Grade retention typically has detrimental effects on student outcomes due to: (1) stigmatization and reduced self-esteem, (2) separation from age-appropriate peers, (3) reduced time to complete education, and (4) potential tracking into lower-ability classes. The literature generally shows that grade retention hurts rather than helps struggling students, despite the intuitive appeal of giving them "another chance" to master the material.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the cutoff in test scores to identify the causal effect.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Students retained due to scoring below the cutoff perform worse on future tests.
